newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends strong on corporate dollar supply.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends strong on corporate dollar supply.

text.p: The Mexican peso gained ground towards the close on late corporate supply of dollars, traders said.
"I feel a local bank settled a hefty trade for some local corporation," a trader said.
"The market held onto their dollars right up to the close, thinking that bank would need to cover short (dollar) positions," he added.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 1.5 and 0.6 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.9420/7.9460 and 7.9390/7.9430 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.5 centavos firmer at 7.9380/7.9430 per dollar.
Dealers stressed that dealing was brisk and volume heavy during the session, and peso strength came as a surprise given the sharp gain in U.S. long bond yields.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were down 26/32 to yield 7.14 percent.
"Despite the (U.S.) long bond, the market was awash with dollars," another trader said.
